look_here_first: Measure several mature leaves and compare intact axillary racemes. Leaves often 10–20 × 5–8 mm; short racemes have crowded flower bases. Do not identify by white flowers or scent alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas native at state level; three qualifying project counties not verified.

morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, usually small oblong or oblanceolate blades; typically entire but some forms toothed.
morphology_keys.racemes: Short, dense, axillary; flower bases close together.
morphology_keys.habit: Branched woody aromatic shrub; axillary leafy fascicles may be present.

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. virgata usually has larger toothed leaves and lax, flexuose racemes; Lantana has rounded heads; Verbena is herbaceous with spikes.
comparisons.cautions: Use multiple mature leaves and flowering axes; leaf teeth, height, scent and flower color alone are unreliable.
